text:
Alex: Heads up — running into flaky 429s when clients re-send streaming requests after a brief network dropout. Two quick Qs: (1) should SDKs surface idempotency-key for streams or rely on resume tokens? (2) recommended backoff when partial stream data may have side-effects? trying to avoid double-applies.
Maria: Streams are messy. Prefer resume tokens for continuing a stream. Idempotency keys are our go-to for non-streaming, discrete ops (create/commit). If a stream maps to server-side side-effects, the server should dedupe when it sees the same Idempotency-Key.
Jay: Client guidance we usually give: exponential backoff with full jitter. start ~200ms, double each retry, cap ~10s, max ~6 attempts. For 429s with Retry-After header honor that first, then resume exponential after the wait. For streams: try resume token first instead of restarting from zero.
Noah: Practical SDK pattern we landed on: send `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` for operations that can be retried safely, and include `Resume-Token` metadata frames for streaming. Example flow:
- client starts stream, server returns resume token periodically
- client on network error: POST /resume with token (or re-open stream with header `Resume-Token`)
If server doesn't support resume, fall back to idempotent server-side dedupe if available.
Alex: Quick follow-up — what about prompt-splitting? some clients chunk very long prompts into N streaming calls. Do we treat each chunk as separate idempotent ops or a single logical op?
Maria: If chunks are independent (e.g., multiple list calls), treat them independently with separate keys. If they're logically one request (splitting for transport), prefer a single idempotency key across chunks and server-side assembly. Otherwise you risk partial completion creating visible side-effects.
Jay: Also, implement a circuit breaker: if a client gets repeated 429s for >1 minute, back off to long sleep (30s-120s) and surface a flaky-network error to the app so it can decide. And avoid retry floods from many clients at once by random jitter.
Noah: Pseudocode for backoff we generally recommend:
```
base = 200ms
attempt = 0
while (attempt < MAX_RETRIES) {
  wait = min(cap, base * 2^attempt)
  wait = random_between(0, wait) // full jitter
  sleep(wait)
  attempt++
}
```
Also: if server sends `Retry-After`, sleep that long (or the header value) before the next attempt; don't add jitter on top of Retry-After.
Alex: Good call. Any language-specific gotchas to call out for SDKs? Node stream reconnects, python async cancellation, etc.
Maria: Node: be careful with automatic re-reads of stream buffer — don't re-send partially-consumed buffers without tracking offsets. Python: ensure cancellation actually closes socket before retrying. Go: prefer context with timeout and explicit resume token handling.
RetryBot: docs snippet: https://redwood.infer/docs/sdk/retries (internal) — includes examples for headers: `Idempotency-Key`, `Resume-Token`, and handling `Retry-After`.
Alex: Thanks — I'll add resume-token tests to the client PR, expose idempotency header in the high-level API, and include backoff/jitter settings. Ping me if you want to review the test matrix. :thumbsup:
